title: Re-Basin-aligned Mirror task deltas
hypothesis: For eight synthetic two-layer ReLU task models that are independently permuted in hidden units, exact Re-Basin alignment will expose six task deltas on a shared two-direction orbit. A one-phase Mirror code should reproduce held-out function outputs with nMSE <=1e-5 and use <=0.90x the actual bytes of the matched direct two-coefficient aligned control; two unrelated tasks test the private-state boundary.
physical_object: shared two-layer ReLU base network plus a shared two-direction output-delta basis
mirror_coordinate: per-task hidden-unit permutation address plus one phase on the aligned delta basis
logical_multiplicity: eight task functions, six aligned to a common low-rank delta orbit and two unrelated private deltas
controls: Re-Basin alignment plus direct two-coefficient delta codes
Re-Basin alignment plus one Mirror phase per aligned task
Re-Basin alignment with private unrelated-task deltas

development.selection_metric: held-out task output nMSE and actual serialized payload bytes

storage.authority: actual deterministic fixed-timestamp ZIP/NPY FP16 inference payload bytes after reload

success_gate: All three fresh seeds: aligned Mirror tasks have output nMSE <=1e-5; total Mirror payload including private deltas and permutations is <=0.90x matched direct aligned coefficient payload; unaligned compression is reported; exact FP16 reload and metric replay.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality in >=2 fresh seeds; or Mirror payload is >=direct aligned coefficients in >=2; or permutation alignment does not improve held-out function reconstruction; or unrelated task functions cannot be retained with the declared private deltas.
boundaries: synthetic post-fit ReLU task functions, not pretrained transformer merge evidence
permutation addresses preserve hidden-unit symmetry and are paid
task coordinates are oracle-generated and not learned
low-rank compression is not independent capacity
Mirror-specific claim requires advantage over Re-Basin plus direct coefficients
